answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake held in escrow, released only after a probationary window of honest work. Creating ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand stakes, and any detected fraud burns the deposit, so mass forgery becomes a losing bet rather than a free echo. Honest participants treat the stake as a kernel of skin in the game: small, verifiable, and expensive to fake at scale, like the pigment that permanently marks dyed cloth and cannot be washed out cheaply.
